author: Jeremiah (prophet)
original: חַי־אָ֘נִי֮ נְאֻם־יְהֹוָה֒ כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה כׇּנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה חוֹתָ֖ם עַל־יַ֣ד יְמִינִ֑י כִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶתְּקֶֽנְךָּ׃ | וּנְתַתִּ֗יךָ בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וּבְיַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה יָג֖וֹר מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַ֥ד הַכַּשְׂדִּֽים׃ | וְהֵטַלְתִּ֣י אֹתְךָ֗ וְאֶֽת־אִמְּךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְלָדַ֔תְךָ עַ֚ל הָאָ֣רֶץ אַחֶ֔רֶת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֻלַּדְתֶּ֖ם שָׁ֑ם וְשָׁ֖ם תָּמֽוּתוּ׃ | וְעַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֛ם מְנַשְּׂאִ֥ים אֶת־נַפְשָׁ֖ם לָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֑ם שָׁ֖מָּה לֹ֥א יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃ {פ}
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria; read from the saved API response.
english: As I live—declares GOD—if you, O King Coniah, son of Jehoiakim, of Judah, were a signet on my right hand, I would tear you off even from there. | I will deliver you into the hands of those who seek your life, into the hands of those you dread, into the hands of King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon and into the hands of the Chaldeans. | I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another land, where you were not born; there you shall both die. | They shall not return to the land that they yearn to come back to.
what_it_says: Jeremiah's oracle against Coniah (Jehoiachin) declares that even as a signet ring on God's hand he would be torn off, and that he and his mother will be exiled to a land not their own, where they will die.
limits: The English gloss 'Coniah (Jeconiah in 24.1)' is a JPS editorial note identifying him with Jehoiachin; the oracle is conditional in form ('if ... were a signet') and says nothing about Joseph or a genealogy.

author: Jeremiah (prophet)
original: הַעֶ֨צֶב נִבְזֶ֜ה נָפ֗וּץ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ כׇּנְיָ֔הוּ אִ֨ם־כְּלִ֔י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֤וּעַ הֽוּטְלוּ֙ ה֣וּא וְזַרְע֔וֹ וְהֻ֨שְׁלְכ֔וּ עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדָֽעוּ׃ | אֶ֥רֶץ אֶ֖רֶץ אָ֑רֶץ שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר־יְהֹוָֽה׃ | כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה כִּתְב֞וּ אֶת־הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ עֲרִירִ֔י גֶּ֖בֶר לֹא־יִצְלַ֣ח בְּיָמָ֑יו כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יִצְלַ֜ח מִזַּרְע֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וּמֹשֵׁ֥ל ע֖וֹד בִּיהוּדָֽה׃ {פ}
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: Is this man Coniah / A wretched broken pot, / A vessel no one wants? / Why are he and his offspring hurled out, / And cast away in a land they knew not? | O land, land, land, / Hear the word of GOD! | Thus said GOD: / Record this man as without succession, / One who shall never be found acceptable; / For none of his offspring shall be accepted / To sit on the throne of David / And to rule again in Judah.
what_it_says: Jeremiah orders the man Coniah recorded as 'without succession' and declares that none of his offspring will sit on David's throne or rule again in Judah.
limits: The text is the core of the 'curse' objection. It speaks of 'his offspring' (zar'o) and of sitting on David's throne; it does not say that a son adopted or born by another line is excluded from a genealogy. The verse is also the one Talmud and midrash later reinterpret (see G4-13 to G4-15).

author: Jeremiah (prophet)
original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה עַל־יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד וְנִבְלָתוֹ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה מֻשְׁלֶ֔כֶת לַחֹ֥רֶב בַּיּ֖וֹם וְלַקֶּ֥רַח בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: Assuredly, thus said GOD concerning King Jehoiakim of Judah: He shall not have any of his line sitting on the throne of David; and his own corpse shall be left exposed to the heat by day and the cold by night.
what_it_says: Jeremiah says of King Jehoiakim, Coniah's father, that none of his line will sit on David's throne and his corpse will be exposed.
limits: The verse is about Jehoiakim (the father), not Coniah; it is cited in Irenaeus III.21.9 as a second curse. Also the Hebrew 'lo-yihyeh-lo yoshev' ('he shall not have one sitting') is a statement about the line, not about adoptive sons.

author: Chronicler (unknown)
original: וּבְנֵי֙ יְכׇנְיָ֣ה אַסִּ֔ר שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֖ל בְּנֽוֹ׃ | וּמַלְכִירָ֥ם וּפְדָיָ֖ה וְשֶׁנְאַצַּ֑ר יְקַמְיָ֥ה הוֹשָׁמָ֖ע וּנְדַבְיָֽה׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: and the sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son, | Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah;
what_it_says: 1 Chronicles 3:17-18 lists Shealtiel as a son of Jeconiah 'the captive', followed by further sons of Jeconiah's line (Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, Nedabiah).
limits: The Hebrew says 'the sons of Jeconiah' (plural) for one named son; 'Assir' (prisoner) is read as a name or epithet. The verse says nothing of Joseph; it shows Shealtiel is a son of Jeconiah, which is the Matthean line.

author: Chronicler (unknown)
original: וּבְנֵ֣י פְדָיָ֔ה זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל וְשִׁמְעִ֑י וּבֶן־זְרֻבָּבֶל֙ מְשֻׁלָּ֣ם וַחֲנַנְיָ֔ה וּשְׁלֹמִ֖ית אֲחוֹתָֽם׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: the sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei; the son[s] of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith was their sister;
what_it_says: 1 Chronicles names Zerubbabel as a son of Pedaiah (not of Shealtiel), which conflicts with Ezra 3:2, Haggai 1:1 and Matthew 1:12 where Zerubbabel is son of Shealtiel.
limits: A harmonization needs Pedaiah as legal father (levirate) or a genealogical gloss; the text itself does not say so. This is a real textual tension to be stated, not hidden.

author: Deuteronomistic historian (unknown)
original: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּמׇלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נְחֻשְׁתָּ֥א בַת־אֶלְנָתָ֖ן מִירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ | וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; his mother’s name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. | He did what was displeasing to GOD, just as his father had done.
what_it_says: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) was eighteen when he became king, reigned three months in Jerusalem, and his mother was Nehushta; he did evil as his father had.
limits: Gives the regnal details. The Hebrew 'Jehoiachin' and the name 'Coniah' in Jer 22 refer to the same king (JPS note). Does not mention a son.

author: Deuteronomistic historian (unknown)
original: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מׇלְכ֗וֹ אֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין מֶלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא׃ | וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־כִּסְא֔וֹ מֵעַ֗ל כִּסֵּ֧א הַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃ | וְשִׁנָּ֕א אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם תָּמִ֛יד לְפָנָ֖יו כׇּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃ | וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה־לּ֛וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Jehoiachin of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, King Evil-merodach of Babylon, in the year he became king, took note of King Jehoiachin of Judah and released him from prison. | He spoke kindly to him, and gave him a throne above those of other kings who were with him in Babylon. | His prison garments were removed, and [Jehoiachin] received regular rations by his favor for the rest of his life. | A regular allotment of food was given him at the king’s behest—an allotment for each day—all the days of his life.
what_it_says: In the 37th year of exile Evil-merodach released Jehoiachin from prison, gave him a seat above other kings and a daily allowance for life.
limits: Shows Jehoiachin alive and honoured in exile; no mention of a son. The Talmud (Sanh 38a, G4-15) connects this period to the 'exile of Jeconiah' still in effect.

author: Haggai (prophet)
original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֣וּא נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֡וֹת אֶ֠קָּחֲךָ֠ זְרֻבָּבֶ֨ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֤ל עַבְדִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ כַּֽחוֹתָ֑ם כִּֽי־בְךָ֣ בָחַ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם יְהֹוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: On that day—declares GOD of Hosts—I will take you, O My servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel—declares GOD—and make you as a signet; for I have chosen you—declares GOD of Hosts.
what_it_says: God will take Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and make him 'as a signet' (chotam), reversing the rejection of Jeconiah in Jer 22:24.
limits: The JPS note says 'bring you close to Me; contrast Jer 22:24-30'. It is an interpretive reversal, not a statement of genealogy; it does not address which genealogy Zerubbabel belongs to.

author: Ezra-Nehemiah compiler (unknown)
original: וַיָּ֩קׇם֩ יֵשׁ֨וּעַ בֶּן־יֽוֹצָדָ֜ק וְאֶחָ֣יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וּזְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיִּבְנ֕וּ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֖ח אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהַעֲל֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ עֹל֔וֹת כַּכָּת֕וּב בְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֥ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
original_edition: Miqra according to the Masorah (MAM), Hebrew digital text on Sefaria (Aleppo Codex based; from he.wikisource); vocalized as on Sefaria.
english: Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brother priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers set to and built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings upon it as is written in the Teaching of Moses, the agent of God.
what_it_says: Zerubbabel is called son of Shealtiel, the same name that Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27 use for Zerubbabel's father.
limits: Ezra does not name Shealtiel's father. Along with Hag 1:1 and 2:23 it fixes 'Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel' as the standard OT description.

author: Targum (anonymous; Jonathan tradition)
original: כִּדְנַן אֲמַר יְיָ כְּתוּבוּ יַת גַבְרָא הָדֵין דְלָא וְלַד גַבְרָא דְלָא יִצְלַח בְּיוֹמוֹהִי אֲרֵי לָא יִצְלַח מִזַרְעֵיהּ גְבַר יָתֵיב עַל כּוּרְסֵי דָוִד וְעָבֵיד שׁוּלְטַן עַל דְבֵית יְהוּדָה:
original_edition: Targum Jonathan, Mikraot Gedolot text as on Sefaria (Aramaic, vocalized); read from the saved API response.
what_it_says: The Aramaic targum renders Jer 22:30 as a command to write this man 'childless' (dela leit lehu gabra) and that no man of his seed shall sit on David's throne.
limits: No English on Sefaria; the Aramaic was read, not translated. The targum keeps the curse wording; it adds no reversal in this verse.

author: Anonymous (compiled Palestine, c. 5th c.)
ref: Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 24:11 (Mandelbaum numbering as on Sefaria)
original: תשובתו של יכניה קבלתי ותשובתכם איני מקבל, שניגזרה עליו גזירה קשה, הד"ה דכת' העצב נבזה נפוץ האיש הזה יכניהו (ירמיה כב:כח).
original_edition: Pesikta de Rav Kahana, Dov Mandelbaum ed. (N.Y. 1987), Oxford MS, as on Sefaria (Hebrew); read from the saved API response.
edition: Mandelbaum ed. (1987) as shown on Sefaria; no English on Sefaria
what_it_says: In the Pesikta's model, God 'accepted' the repentance of a person under a harsh decree (Cain, Ahab, and Jeconiah, whose decree is Jer 22:28, 'a broken vessel'); the passage is a case of repentance softening a decree, not a case of the curse being fully lifted.
limits: The excerpt is the opening of the argument, with Cain and Ahab as parallels; the R. Meir line that God swore (Jer 22:24) that no king would be established from Jeconiah is later in the same piska and not in this item. No English read, so status PARTLY.

author: Anonymous (compiled Palestine, c. 5th c.)
original: גדול כחה של תשובה שביטלה את השבועה וביטלה את הגזירה. ביטלה את השבועה מנין, חי אני נאם י"י כי אם יהיה כניהו בן יהויקים וג' (שם כד), וכת' ביום ההוא נאם י"י צבאות אקחך זרובבל בן שלתיאל וג' (חגי ב:כג). ביטלה את הגזירה מנין, כה אמ' י"י כתבו את האיש הזה ערירי וג' (ירמיה כב:ל). ובני יכניה אסיר וג' (ד"ה א' ג:יז)
original_edition: Pesikta de Rav Kahana, Mandelbaum ed. (1987) as on Sefaria; read from the saved API response.
edition: Mandelbaum ed. (1987) as shown on Sefaria; no English on Sefaria
what_it_says: Repentance annuls both the oath (Jer 22:24, with Hag 2:23 as the reversal) and the decree (Jer 22:30, with 1 Chr 3:17), as proved from the texts quoted.
limits: Midrashic argument for the lifting of the curse by repentance; it is not a claim about genealogy and states no Matthean or Lukan line.

author: Anonymous midrash (c. 5th c. AD, Palestine)
original: גָּדוֹל הוּא כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְבַטֶּלֶת גְּזֵרָה וּמְבַטֶּלֶת שְׁבוּעָה, שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (נחמיה כב, כד): חַי אָנִי נְאֻם ה' כִּי אִם יִהְיֶה כָּנְיָהוּ בֶן יְהוֹיָקִים וגו', וּמְבַטֶּלֶת גְּזֵרָה, (נחמיה כב, ל): כֹּה אָמַר ה' כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי, וּכְתִיב (דברי הימים א ג, יז): וּבְנֵי יְכָנְיָה אַסִּר [בנו] שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל בְּנוֹ, אַסִּר, שֶׁהָיָה בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִים, שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל בְּנוֹ, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הוּשְׁתְּלָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד.
original_edition: Midrash Rabbah, Hebrew text on Sefaria (Midrash Rabbah -- TE, as labelled on Sefaria); read from the saved API response.
english: Rabbi Aḥa and Rabbi Avin bar Binyamin in the name of Rabbi Abba: Great is the power of repentance, and it voids an edict and voids an oath. An oath, as it is stated: “As I live, the utterance of the Lord, for if Konya, son of Yehoyakim, [king of Judah, would be a signet ring upon My right hand, then from there I would sever you]” (Jeremiah 22:24). It voids an edict: “Write this man childless, a man who will not succeed in his days,” and it is written: “The sons of Konya, Asir, She’altiel his son” (I Chronicles 3:17); Asir, because he was in prison [beit haasurim]; She’altiel, because the kingdom of the house of David was planted [hushtela] from him.
translator: Sefaria Midrash Rabbah English (2022); translator not named in the Sefaria record
edition: The Sefaria Midrash Rabbah, 2022 (English); Midrash Rabbah TE (Hebrew, as on Sefaria)
what_it_says: Rabbi Aha and R. Avin in the name of R. Abba: repentance voids an edict and voids an oath; the oath of Jer 22:24 and the edict of Jer 22:30 are cited, and I Chr 3:17 shows the edict voided.
limits: Sefaria's Hebrew cites the Jer 22:24 verse with the book-name 'נחמיה' (Nehemiah) in a parenthetical reference, an apparent typo; the verse text quoted is Jeremiah. Midrashic, not historical.

author: Talmudic rabbis (Amoraim)
original: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: גָּלוּת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל הַכֹּל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ כִּתְבוּ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה עֲרִירִי גֶּבֶר לֹא יִצְלַח בְּיָמָיו כִּי לֹא יִצְלַח מִזַּרְעוֹ אִישׁ יֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דָוִד וּמֹשֵׁל עוֹד בִּיהוּדָה״. וּבָתַר דִּגְלָה כְּתִיב: ״וּבְנֵי יְכָנְיָה אַסִּר (בְּנוֹ) שַׁלְתִּיאֵל בְּנו
original_edition: Talmud Bavli, Sanhedrin 37b, William Davidson vocalized Aramaic edition as on Sefaria (Hebrew/Aramaic); read from the saved API response.
english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Exile atones for all transgressions and renders a sinner like a new person, as it is stated concerning the king Jeconiah, a descendant of King David: “So says the Lord: Write you this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days; for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling anymore in Judah” (Jeremiah 22:30). And after Jeconiah was exiled it is written: “And the sons of Jeconiah, the same is Assir, Shealtiel his son” (I Chronicles 3:17).
translator: Koren Talmud Bavli (Noé edition), English as on Sefaria (Sefaria label: William Davidson Edition - English; versionSource: Koren)
edition: Sefaria: William Davidson vocalized Aramaic / Koren Noé English
what_it_says: R. Yohanan: exile atones for everything, citing Jer 22:30 ('write this man childless'); after the exile, I Chr 3:17 lists Jeconiah's son Shealtiel, whose birth the Gemara explains.
limits: The statement is that exile atones, not that the curse on Jeconiah's seed is lifted. Sefaria English is a modern translation, not a 19th c. text. Folio cited from Sefaria; not checked against a printed Vilna page.

author: Talmudic rabbis (Amoraim)
original: אִין, צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִקְדִּים גָּלוּת צִדְקִיָּהוּ וְעוֹד גָּלוּת יְכׇנְיָה קַיֶּימֶת. דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ בְּגָלוּת יְכׇנְיָה: ״הֶחָרָשׁ וְהַמַּסְגֵּר אֶלֶף
original_edition: Talmud Bavli, Sanhedrin 38a, William Davidson vocalized Aramaic edition as on Sefaria; read from the saved API response.
english: Yes, because it was a righteous act that the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed for the Jewish people by hastening the exile of Zedekiah while the Jews who had been exiled in the exile of Jeconiah, which preceded it, were still alive, as the wise people among those exiled with Jeconiah were able to instruct those exiled with Zedekiah.
translator: Koren Talmud Bavli (Noé edition), English as on Sefaria (versionSource: Koren)
edition: Sefaria: William Davidson vocalized Aramaic / Koren Noé English
what_it_says: God hastened the exile of Zedekiah as a mercy, because Jeconiah's exile was still in effect and the Jews already exiled with Jeconiah could teach those exiled with Zedekiah.
limits: Shows the Talmud treating Jeconiah's exile as an ongoing chronological marker, not as a curse lifted. Does not discuss genealogy.

author: Matthew (traditional)
original: Ἰωσείας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος. Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβάβελ,
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, Text (1881), read visually from the PDF page image at 200 dpi (PDF p. 14); the PDF text layer agrees on the words. Accent marks as read from the image.
english: And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon: | And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;
translator: King James Version (1611) wording, as shown on Bible Hub interlinear (biblehub.com/interlinear/matthew/1-11.htm and 1-12.htm)
edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 (Macmillan, Cambridge); scan on archive.org (newtestamentinor1881west)
what_it_says: Matthew says Josiah begat Jechoniah at the Babylonian exile, and after the exile Jechoniah begat Shealtiel, who begat Zerubbabel.
limits: Matthew's 'Jechonias' is Coniah/Jeconiah of Jer 22 (son of Jehoiakim); Matthew omits Jehoiakim from 'Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren', a known skip. Matthew makes Shealtiel the son of Jechonias, which is the Josephite link to the curse. The curse of Jer 22:30 is not discussed in Matthew.

author: Luke (traditional)
original: τοῦ Ἰωανάν τοῦ Ῥησά τοῦ Ζοροβάβελ τοῦ Σαλαθιήλ τοῦ Νηρεί, 28 τοῦ Μελχεί τοῦ Ἀδδεί τοῦ Κωσάμ τοῦ Ἐλμαδάμ τοῦ Ἤρ
original_edition: Westcott & Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek, Text (1881), read visually from the PDF page image at 200 dpi (PDF p. 134); accents read from the image (biblehub interlinear, GMS, gives Ἰωανὰν, Ῥησὰ, Σαλαθιὴλ, Νηρὶ).
english: Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri, | Which was the son of Melchi, which was the son of Addi, which was the son of Cosam, which was the son of Elmodam, which was the son of Er,
translator: King James Version (1611) wording, as shown on Bible Hub interlinear (biblehub.com/interlinear/luke/3-27.htm and 3-28.htm)
edition: Westcott & Hort 1881 (Macmillan, Cambridge); scan on archive.org (newtestamentinor1881west)
what_it_says: Luke's list goes Zorobabel, Salathiel, Neri: Salathiel is the son of Neri, not of Jeconiah. The names Zorobabel and Salathiel recur, with different fathers.
limits: The Greek text does not say which Salathiel is meant beyond the father 'Neri'; no reference to Jeconiah in Luke. The Lukan line passes through Nathan, not Solomon (not in this item).

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
ref: Adversus haereses III.21.9 (ANF/Massuet division; Harvey's own chapter heading is CAP. XXIX, 'Ostensio quoniam, si Joseph filius fuisset Dominus, non rex esse potuisset')
original: Super hæc autem nec rex esse posset, si quidem Joseph filius fuisset; nec hæres, secundum Hieremiam. Joseph enim Joacim et Jechoniæ filius ostenditur, quemadmodum et Matthæus generationem ejus exponit. Jechonias autem, et qui ab eo omnes, abdicati sunt a regno, Hieremia dicente sic: Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, si factus fuerit Jechonias filius Joacim, rex Juda, signaculum in manu dextera mea, inde abstraham eum, et tradam eum in manu quærentium animam tuam. Et iterum:
original_edition: W. W. Harvey (ed.), Sancti Irenaei episcopi Lugdunensis Libros quinque adversus haereses, vol. 2 (Cambridge, 1857), Latin text with Harvey's apparatus; read from the PDF image (PDF p. 130) and the archive.org djvu OCR (sanctiirenaeiep00harvgoog)
english: 9. But besides, if indeed He had been the son of Joseph, He could not, according to Jeremiah, be either king or heir. For Joseph is shown to be the son of Joachim and Jechoniah, as also Matthew sets forth in his pedigree. Matthew 1:12-16 But Jechoniah, and all his posterity, were disinherited from the kingdom; Jeremiah thus declaring, As I live, says the Lord, if Jechoniah the son of Joachim king of Judah had been made the signet of my right hand, I would pluck him thence, and deliver him into the hand of those seeking your life. Jeremiah 22:24-25
translator: Alexander Roberts and William Rambaut, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (Buffalo 1885), as on newadvent.org/fathers/0103321.htm
edition: Harvey 1857 (vol. 2); ANF vol. 1 (1885) via New Advent
what_it_says: Irenaeus argues that if Jesus were Joseph's son he could not be king, because Joseph is shown (in Matthew's pedigree) to be the son of Joachim and Jechoniah, and Jechoniah's line was disinherited.
limits: Irenaeus writes that Matthew 'sets forth' Joseph's pedigree; he does not discuss Luke 3 at this point. Matthew = Joseph is thus attested in the second century, not invented in 1500.

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
original: Inhonoratus est Jechonias, quemadmodum vas quod non est opus, quoniam projectus est in terram, quam non sciebat. Terra audi sermonem Domini: scribe virum hunc abdicatum hominem, quoniam non augebit de semine ejus sedens super thronum David, princeps in Juda. Et iterum Deus ait super Joacim patrem ejus: Propter hoc sic dicit Dominus super Joacim patrem ejus, regem Judaeae: Non enim erit ex eo sedens super thronum David; et mortificatum ejus erit projectum in æstu diei, et in glacie noctis, et respiciam super eum, et super filios ejus, et inferam super eos, et super inhabitantes Hierusalem, super terram Juda, omnia mala, quæ locutus sum super eos.
original_edition: W. W. Harvey (ed.), Sancti Irenaei episcopi Lugdunensis Libros quinque adversus haereses, vol. 2 (Cambridge, 1857), Latin text with Harvey's apparatus; read from the PDF image (PDF p. 130) and the archive.org djvu OCR (sanctiirenaeiep00harvgoog). Harvey's note 4 gives 'mortificatum ejus' as Greek τὸ θνησιμαῖον αὐτοῦ, a gloss, not an Irenaeus Greek text.
english: And again: Jechoniah is dishonoured as a useless vessel, for he has been cast into a land which he knew not. Earth, hear the word of the Lord: Write this man a disinherited person; for none of his seed, sitting on the throne of David, shall prosper, or be a prince in Judah. Jeremiah 22:28 And again, God speaks of Joachim his father: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Joachim his father, king of Judea, There shall be from him none sitting upon the throne of David: and his dead body shall be cast out in the heat of day, and in the frost of night. And I will look upon him, and upon his sons, and will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, upon the land of Judah, all the evils that I have pronounced against them. Jeremiah 36:30-31
translator: Alexander Roberts and William Rambaut, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (Buffalo 1885), as on newadvent.org/fathers/0103321.htm
edition: Harvey 1857 (vol. 2); ANF vol. 1 (1885) via New Advent
what_it_says: Irenaeus quotes the rejection of Jeconiah (Jer 22:28) and of Jehoiakim (Jer 36:30-31) to show that no descendant of Jehoiakim's line sits on David's throne.
limits: The Latin is an old Latin translation of Irenaeus (Greek original lost for this book). Harvey's text is printed with apparatus; the OCR of 'Judaeae' is confirmed on the page image.

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
original: Qui ergo eum dicunt ex Joseph generatum, et in eo habere spem, abdicatos se faciunt a regno, sub maledictione et increpatione decidentes, quæ erga Jechoniam et in semen ejus. Propter hoc enim dicta sunt hæc de Jechonia, Spiritu præsciente ea quæ a malis doctoribus dicuntur; uti discant, quoniam ex semine ejus, id est ex Joseph, non erit natus, sed secundum repromissionem Dei de ventre David suscitatur Rex æternus, qui recapitulatur omnia in se.
original_edition: W. W. Harvey (ed.), Sancti Irenaei episcopi Lugdunensis Libros quinque adversus haereses, vol. 2 (Cambridge, 1857), Latin text with Harvey's apparatus; read from the PDF image (PDF p. 130) and the archive.org djvu OCR (sanctiirenaeiep00harvgoog)
english: Those, therefore, who say that He was begotten of Joseph, and that they have hope in Him, do cause themselves to be disinherited from the kingdom, failing under the curse and rebuke directed against Jechoniah and his seed. Because for this reason have these things been spoken concerning Jechoniah, the [Holy] Spirit foreknowing the doctrines of the evil teachers; that they may learn that from his seed — that is, from Joseph — He was not to be born but that, according to the promise of God, from David's belly the King eternal is raised up, who sums up all things in Himself, and has gathered into Himself the ancient formation [of man].
translator: Alexander Roberts and William Rambaut, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (Buffalo 1885), as on newadvent.org/fathers/0103321.htm
edition: Harvey 1857 (vol. 2); ANF vol. 1 (1885) via New Advent
what_it_says: Irenaeus concludes that those who say Christ was begotten of Joseph disinherit themselves; Christ is born 'from David's belly' by God's promise and not from Joseph's seed.
limits: The phrase 'de ventre David' is the nearest Irenaeus comes to a Davidic line through Mary; this passage does not name Mary, Heli or Luke. It is the earliest explicit use of the Jeconiah curse against a Josephite Messiah that we have located in this pass.

author: Jerome (Eusebius Hieronymus)
ref: Commentarius in Matthaeum I, on Matt 1:12 (Latin Vulgate 'Et post transmigrationem Babylonis')
original: Et post transmgrationem BubyiO' ni$, Jechonia$ genuit Satathiet. Satathiel autem genuit Zorobabet. Zorobabet autem genuit Abiud. Abiud autem genuit Eliacim, Eiiacim autem genuit Azor. A%or autem 11 g^^it Sadoc. Sadoc autem genuit Achim, Achim autem genuit Etiud. Eliud autem genuit Eleazar. Eleaxar autem genuit Matthan. Matthan autem genuit /aco6. Sivoluerimus Jeclioniam in fineprimas tessa- rescedecadis [Al. tesseradecadis] ponere, in sequenti non erunt quatuordecim » sed tredecim. Sciamus Sgitur, Jechoniam priorem ipsum esse quem et « Joa- cim : sccundum autem, filium, uon patrem : quorum
original_edition: Migne, Patrologia Latina 26 (Paris 1844), col. 24 (running head), read from archive.org djvu OCR (patrologiaecurs240unkngoog). OCR only; the PDF (63 MB) exceeds the 60 MB limit and was not downloaded, so no image check. OCR errors left uncorrected.
page: PL 26, col. 24 (from OCR running head; not checked on image)
what_it_says: Per the OCR: if Jechonias is put at the end of the first fourteen, the second group has thirteen; Jechonias the earlier is the same man as Joachim, and the later one is his son, not his father.
limits: OCR is noisy and unverified; no English read. Jerome treats the 14x3 count as a problem to be solved by identifying Jechonias with Joachim; he does not say Matthew gives Mary's line.

author: Jerome (Eusebius Hieronymus)
ref: Commentarius in Matthaeum I, on Matt 1:16-18 (Joseph's pedigree and Mary's tribe)
original: Gum Josepli non sit pater Domiui Salvatoris , 12 quid pertinet ad Dominiim genera- tionis ordo deductus usque ad Joseph ? Cui respoii- debimus primum , non esse consuetudiiiis Scriptu- rarum, ui mulierum in generationibus ordo tezatur. Deinde ez una iribu fuisse Joseph et Mariam : unde ez Lege eam accipere cogebatur ut propinquam , et quod simul censetur iii Bethleem, ut de una videlicet siirpe generaii.
original_edition: Migne PL 26 (1844), col. approx. 24-25, archive.org djvu OCR (patrologiaecurs240unkngoog). OCR only; no image check; OCR errors left uncorrected.
page: PL 26, col. approx. 24-25 (not checked on image)
what_it_says: Per the OCR: since Joseph is not the Lord's father, why trace the Lord's line to Joseph? Jerome answers that Joseph and Mary were of one tribe and one stock, so Mary is a kinswoman under the Law.
limits: This is the closest witness in this item set to 'Mary of the same tribe and stock' (ca. 400 AD). It does not say Mary descends from David explicitly, nor that Luke's list is Mary's. OCR only.
